- id: file:human/CDH1/CDH1-uniprot.txt
  title: UniProt record for human CDH1 (P12830)
  findings:
  - statement: Cadherins, including E-cadherin/CDH1, are calcium-dependent cell adhesion proteins.
  - statement: E-cadherin mediates homophilic cell-cell adhesion by preferentially interacting
      with itself.
  - statement: E-cadherin is a component of an E-cadherin/catenin adhesion complex containing
      beta-catenin or gamma-catenin, located at adherens junctions.
- id: file:human/CDH1/CDH1-deep-research-manual.md
  title: Manual deep research summary for human CDH1 (E-cadherin)
  findings:
  - statement: E-cadherin mediates calcium-dependent homophilic trans-adhesion via strand-swap
      dimerization between EC1 domains on apposing cells; trans interactions are sufficient
      for aggregation while cis interactions are additionally required for junction assembly.
  - statement: The cytoplasmic tail of E-cadherin nucleates the cadherin-catenin complex by
      binding beta-catenin/plakoglobin and p120-catenin, coupling homophilic adhesion to the
      cortical actin cytoskeleton via alpha-catenin and adaptor proteins.
- id: file:human/CDH1/CDH1-deep-research-falcon.md
  title: Falcon deep research report on CDH1
  findings:
  - statement: E-cadherin is a calcium-dependent cell-cell adhesion molecule that organizes
      epithelial tissue architecture via homophilic adhesion, supporting epithelial integrity
      and polarity.
  - statement: The E-cadherin ectodomain is composed of five extracellular cadherin repeats
      (EC1-EC5) containing calcium-binding sites that rigidify the ectodomain for adhesion.
  - statement: Homophilic adhesion proceeds through an EC1-mediated X-dimer intermediate to
      a stable strand-swapped dimer in which a tryptophan from one EC1 inserts into the hydrophobic
      pocket of the opposing EC1.
  - statement: In epithelia, E-cadherin is enriched at the plasma membrane and concentrates
      at adherens junctions, where it maintains epithelial sheet cohesion and tissue architecture.
  - statement: The E-cadherin cytoplasmic tail is anchored to the actin cytoskeleton through
      beta-catenin and alpha-catenin, enabling transmission of actomyosin forces across junctions.
  - statement: E-cadherin also interacts with p120-catenin, and changes in E-cadherin availability
      can alter beta-catenin and p120-catenin signaling states.
  - statement: Adherens junctions formed by E-cadherin act as a mechanosensitive scaffold,
      transmitting actomyosin-generated pulling forces via beta-catenin/alpha-catenin anchorage
      rather than functioning as static "glue".
  - statement: Loss or downregulation of E-cadherin can release beta-catenin to permit nuclear
      translocation and Wnt pathway activation, and can alter RhoA/Rac1 signaling via redistribution
      of p120-catenin.
  - statement: EMT programs repress E-cadherin, and this loss contributes to invasion and
      metastasis; E-cadherin downregulation is a hallmark of EMT and cancer cell motility
      changes.
  - statement: Germline CDH1 pathogenic variants are a primary cause of hereditary diffuse
      gastric cancer (HDGC), with clinical management historically including prophylactic
      total gastrectomy.
  - statement: E-cadherin loss is necessary but not sufficient for invasive progression; invasion
      in HDGC models emerges from the interplay between defective cell-cell junctions, ECM
      attachment, and 3D tissue architecture.
  - statement: E-cadherin can undergo proteolytic cleavage/shedding, generating soluble E-cadherin
      fragments; cleavage releases junctional restraint and can free beta-catenin.

- id: PMID:18273011
  title: The genome of the choanoflagellate Monosiga brevicollis and the origin of metazoans.
  findings:
  - statement: The choanoflagellate M. brevicollis encodes at least 23 cadherin-domain proteins.
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: PubMed-verified (King et al. 2008 Nature); full text cached. Establishes
      that cadherin-domain proteins predate animals; says nothing about classical cadherins
      or catenin binding.
- id: PMID:18276888
  title: The premetazoan ancestry of cadherins.
  findings:
  - statement: Choanoflagellates have about as many cadherin genes as complex animals.
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: PubMed-verified (Abedin & King 2008 Science 319:946). Abstract only in cache
      (no PMC full text), so domain-level claims about the choanoflagellate cadherins are
      not taken from this paper.
- id: PMID:22837400
  title: Origin of metazoan cadherin diversity and the antiquity of the classical cadherin/β-catenin
    complex.
  findings:
  - statement: Classical cadherins are an animal innovation, unlike the lefftyrin, coherin
      and hedgling families shared with choanoflagellates.
  - statement: A sponge classical cadherin keeps the cytoplasmic residues used to bind beta-catenin,
      and sponge beta-catenin recovered it in a yeast two-hybrid screen.
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: PubMed-verified (Nichols et al. 2012 PNAS); full text cached. Key evidence
      that classical cadherins and the beta-catenin-binding cytoplasmic domain are animal-specific;
      the sponge interaction is predicted plus Y2H, not shown in vivo.
- id: PMID:20817718
  title: New insights into the evolution of metazoan cadherins.
  findings:
  - statement: The classical cadherin cytoplasmic domain that binds p120-catenin and beta-catenin
      is conserved from placozoans to humans.
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: PubMed-verified (Hulpiau & van Roy 2011 Mol Biol Evol). Abstract only in
      cache; sequence-based survey of animal cadherin repertoires.
- id: PMID:27189570
  title: Characterization of the Cadherin-Catenin Complex of the Sea Anemone Nematostella
    vectensis and Implications for the Evolution of Metazoan Cell-Cell Adhesion.
  findings:
  - statement: Sea anemone classical cadherins bind sea anemone beta-catenin with nanomolar
      affinity, and the alpha/beta-catenin heterodimer binds them.
  - statement: Choanoflagellates lack classical cadherins.
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: PubMed-verified (Clarke et al. 2016 Mol Biol Evol); full text cached. Direct
      biochemical evidence that the cadherin-beta-catenin interaction is conserved in a non-bilaterian
      animal.
- id: PMID:30629955
  title: The cadherin-catenin complex is necessary for cell adhesion and embryogenesis in
    Nematostella vectensis.
  findings:
  - statement: The cadherin-catenin complex is required for calcium-dependent cell-cell adhesion
      in sea anemone embryos.
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: PubMed-verified (Clarke, Lowe & Nelson 2019 Dev Biol); full text cached.
      Functional (alpha-catenin knockdown, calcium-dependent aggregation) evidence in a cnidarian;
      cadherin itself was not knocked down.

- id: PMID:21186356
  title: APC(Cdh1) mediates EphA4-dependent downregulation of AMPA receptors in homeostatic

  reference_review:

- id: PMID:19340315
  title: HD-PTP is a catalytically inactive tyrosine phosphatase due to a conserved divergence
    in its phosphatase domain.
  reference_review:
    relevance: MEDIUM
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: 'Genuine normal full-text cache read, including Results/Figures 1–4: human
      PTPN23 WT is inactive against tested DiFMUP/pNPP substrates and S1394A restores activity.

- id: PMID:10963665
  title: A role for alpha-and beta-catenins in bacterial uptake.
  reference_review:
    relevance: HIGH
    correctness: VERIFIED
    review_notes: 'Authentic normal cache is abstract-only. Selected full primary PMC27655
      Methods, Results and legends were independently read externally: human E-cadherin variants
      in L2071 cells, cytoplasmic deletion and human/mouse alpha-catenin chimera, plus human
      epithelial-cell recruitment. Supports receptor coupling for InlA-mediated uptake, independently
      of the original rat Bifidobacterium source.'

suggested_questions:
- question: Which E-cadherin activities in neurons are supported by cadherin-specific constructs,
    independently of the unrelated APC/C coactivator FZR1 also called Cdh1?
- question: Can the exact original CDH1/CD46, Src, Armus and perinuclear-localization assays
    be recovered to resolve the remaining source-specific uncertainties?
- question: How do regulated cleavage and trafficking change the contribution of intracellular
    E-cadherin fragments to catenin signaling?
